Simulate a steady-state, two-phase (oil–water) flow in a horizontal pipe using twoPhaseEulerFoam in OpenFOAM.
The pipe has a diameter of 0.05 m and a length of 2 m to allow the flow to fully develop.
At the inlet, impose a fixed mixture velocity of 1 m/s applied as a uniform fixedValue in both `U` and `U.water`, so there is no slip velocity between the phases.
At the inlet, set the water volume fraction as `alpha.water = 0.3` using a uniform fixedValue.
At the walls, apply `noSlip` velocity boundary conditions for both phases.
At the outlet, apply `zeroGradient` boundary conditions for both `U` and `U.water`.
In `0/alpha.water`, set the outlet as `zeroGradient` with the initial value `uniform 0.3`; do not use `fixedValue` at the outlet.
At the outlet, apply a fixed static pressure boundary condition with `fixedValue` and `value uniform 0` for the pressure field.
Use standard water properties for the water phase: density 1000 kg/m³ and dynamic viscosity 0.001 Pa·s.
Use typical light oil properties for the oil phase: density 850 kg/m³ and dynamic viscosity 0.008 Pa·s.
Include gravity in the simulation with magnitude 9.81 m/s² acting in the negative Z direction, so the phases can naturally stratify in the horizontal pipe.
Treat the flow as turbulent using the standard k-epsilon (`kEpsilon`) turbulence model, which is compatible with the `noSlip` wall conditions and wall functions.
Run the case to steady state using `twoPhaseEulerFoam`.
